Do not commit yet.
Before we move on, there is one architectural refinement I want to make.
Current decomposition
spatial/
├── data.ts
├── types.ts
├── accent.ts
├── StageNode.tsx
├── KnowledgePacketNode.tsx
...
This is good, but I would not stop there.
Because this canvas is going to become the live operational model of Knowledge Operations, I would split it into layers:
knowledge-v3/
└── spatial/
    ├── model/
    │   ├── types.ts
    │   ├── graph.ts
    │   ├── packets.ts
    │   ├── routes.ts
    │   └── stages.ts
    │
    ├── engine/
    │   ├── KnowledgeFlowEngine.tsx
    │   ├── PacketAnimator.tsx
    │   ├── RouteLayer.tsx
    │   ├── SelectionEngine.ts
    │   └── CameraEngine.ts
    │
    ├── components/
    │   ├── StageNode.tsx
    │   ├── KnowledgePacket.tsx
    │   ├── Background.tsx
    │   ├── Overlay.tsx
    │   ├── Controls.tsx
    │   ├── MetricsBadge.tsx
    │   └── SelectionSummary.tsx
    │
    ├── hooks/
    │   ├── useCamera.ts
    │   ├── useKnowledgeSelection.ts
    │   ├── useKnowledgeFlow.ts
    │   └── useSpatialGraph.ts
    │
    └── SpatialCanvas.tsx
I recommend this because the current canvas is only the beginning. Based on the roadmap we've been building, it will eventually support:


thousands of knowledge objects,


live runtime events,


graph navigation,


zoom and pan,


clustering,


filtering,


search,


lineage visualization,


replay,


playback,


runtime synchronization,


collaborative cursors.


Treating it as a small feature now will force a second refactor later. Building it as a miniature subsystem from the start aligns better with the production-grade architecture you've been applying across KoreLumina.

The terminal shows types.ts is complete. The implementation stopped before data.ts was created.
